public_rationale: Nature reported persistent hallucinations on 22 April 2026, but continuing errors do not establish permanent inability to achieve practical reliability [e1]. A preprint released on 19 October 2026 reported that Falcon, one of ten models tested on 70 academic prompts in February 2025, achieved zero hallucinations but had the lowest recall and highest response deviation [e2]. This narrow result does not demonstrate broad reliability with useful answer coverage and independent replication [e2]. TrueStandard's October 2026 tests found fabricated sources from every tested model on difficult health and science questions without web access [e3]. These findings establish neither permanent impossibility nor the broad, independently replicated reliability required to resolve the forecast [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: The Nature paper does not establish impossibility across future systems and uses [e1].
Falcon's zero-hallucination result covers one narrow benchmark, with low recall and no independent replication supplied [e2].
TrueStandard tested source generation on 100 difficult health and science questions without web access. This does not establish reliability across ordinary factual and professional work [e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Gary Marcus restates that the output of generative AI will never be trustworthy.

statement.excerpt: And how I kept saying you’d never be able to trust the output of GenAI?
statement.document_title: Why is the ROI on Generative AI so poor?

from_speaker: you’d never be able to trust
our_interpretation: Read as a continuing prediction about generative AI reliability, rather than a claim about whether Marcus previously said these words.
The plain reading is that users will never be able to rely on generative AI output in ordinary factual and professional work without routinely checking its correctness.
Trust means practical reliability appropriate to the task, not mathematical perfection on every possible input.
Marcus supplies neither a numerical reliability threshold nor a deadline. No numerical cutoff is attributed to him.
criteria.support_condition: A conclusive demonstration that generative AI cannot attain practical reliability under this reading, with assumptions covering the claimed technology and uses. Continuing errors in existing systems alone cannot establish 'never'.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A dated, independently replicated demonstration that generative AI output can reliably be used without routine external verification across representative factual and professional tasks, with useful answer coverage and errors appropriate to those tasks.

evidence.explanation: The paper describes persistent hallucinations at publication and proposes changes to evaluation incentives. Existing failures establish neither permanent impossibility nor a decisive reliability breakthrough.

The authors report zero hallucinations on a 70-prompt academic test conducted in February 2025, with poor completeness. This challenges the idea that every evaluation must show hallucinations, but does not demonstrate broad practical trustworthiness.

evidence.excerpt: Every model here made up sources on these questions.
evidence.explanation: The publisher tested source generation on 100 difficult health and science questions without web access and reports fabricated sources from every tested model. This documents a continuing, bounded reliability problem, not a permanent limit on generative AI.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An independently replicated demonstration of reliable use without routine external verification across representative factual and professional tasks, measuring correctness, serious errors, abstention and useful answer coverage; or a conclusive impossibility result covering the claimed technology and uses beyond restricted training assumptions.
